question_text: A machine fills bottles with tomato sauce. Each bottle is filled independently of all other bottles. The volume of sauce in each bottle is normally distributed with mean $500\text{ mL}$ and standard deviation $2.5\text{ mL}$. Bottles are deemed to require extra sauce if the machine delivers less than $495\text{ mL}$.

subparts.stem: Calculate the probability that a randomly selected bottle requires extra sauce.

mark_breakdown.desc: Defining random variable $X \sim \text{N}(500, (2.5)^2)$ and writing probability expression $P(X < 495)$

subparts.solution:
Let the volume of sauce in a randomly selected bottle be $X\text{ mL}$.

$X \sim \text{N}(500, (2.5)^2)$

$\therefore P(X < 495) \approx 0.022750 \approx 0.0228$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Cumulative distribution function for a normal variable $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$.
step_by_step: Calculate lower-tail probability $P(X < 495)$ using Normal CDF with lower bound $-\infty$ and upper bound $495$.

subparts.stem: From a sample of 200 bottles, calculate the probability that at least 8 bottles require extra sauce.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Binomial distribution model where each trial is independent with a constant probability of success found from part a.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using rounded probability from part a prematurely, leading to rounding inaccuracies.
